title: dreikoerper: a search engine for periodic orbits of the planar three-body problem, and its finds
description:
A search engine for periodic orbits of the planar three-body problem with zero angular momentum (G = 1), the orbits it found that are in none of the published lists, and a 30-digit verification of each one, with linear stability from the monodromy matrix.

Main result: a linearly stable orbit at masses 1 : 1 : 4 in the isosceles collinear (Euler) configuration, a = 0.80329455331149897894751545304123, b = 1.43593335078306727053457398659518, T = 53.25485430443248007068935995289679, stability indices 0.0501 and −0.0599. It is not in Li, Jing & Liao (2018) and not a k-fold satellite of any orbit in that list. It is the continuation in m3 of the orbit I.A-5 that this list gives at masses 1 : 1 : 2, so it is a new, stable member of a listed family; along the family it is stable for m3 from about 3.74 to 4.18 (30-digit samples). The data package (fundbericht/) holds 686 orbits outside the lists, each verified to 30 digits. The script bahn-pruefen.mjs re-checks the stable orbit without any downloads.

The published lists of other authors are not included; daten-holen.mjs fetches them from their sources and checks each file by SHA-256.
notes: Code: MIT. Results and data package (ergebnisse/, fundbericht/): CC BY 4.0. Felix Habl had the idea and directed the work; the code, the computations and the documentation were written by Claude, an AI model by Anthropic, in conversation with him. Every number comes from a computation in this code.
